tc1.title: TC1 - Normal load (~70 %)
tc1.desc: Baseline: link is not congested. Every scheduler should meet all SLAs.

tc2.title: TC2 - Heavy congestion (~170 % offered load)
tc2.desc: Bulk traffic overloads the 10 Mbps bottleneck. FIFO must fail emergency/voice SLAs.

tc3.title: TC3 - Disaster surge: emergency burst during congestion
tc3.desc: 20 emergency sources raise 60 pps each for 6 s while bulk traffic saturates the link.

tc4.title: TC4 - Failure: 2 s link outage and recovery
tc4.desc: Link goes down 8-10 s with an emergency event in progress. Measures loss and recovery time.

tc5.title: TC5 - Failure: capacity degradation to 35 % (6-14 s)
tc5.desc: E.g. microwave link fade / backup link. Priority classes must survive, video degrades.

tc6.title: TC6 - Attack: bulk flow falsely marked as emergency (8 Mbps)
tc6.desc: Spoofed DSCP-48 / QEP class-0 flood. Strict priority collapses; policed EPS must hold.

tc7.title: TC7 - Noisy markings (DSCP stripped 25 %, wrong port 10 %, header on 80 %)
tc7.desc: Classifier robustness under congestion; compare classifier ablation (accuracy).

tc8.title: TC8 - Starvation test: voice over-subscription (90 calls)
tc8.desc: Strict priority starves video/bulk completely; EPS bounds voice to its reservation.

tc9.title: TC9 - Lossy link (2 % random loss, moderate load)
tc9.desc: Isolates link loss from congestion loss; delay must be unaffected.
